content:
sre-bot: ALERT: tokenization-service (eu-west-1) high error rate + tail latency. 5xx_rate > 2% over 5m, p99 latency spiking. Page: @michelle. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/12345 :rotating_light:

michelle: ack — on it. opening bridge in 2.

michelle: quick snapshot — looks like a pathological case in the tokenizer batcher. p95 bursts on long inputs. impacts streaming for hosted customers, some calls time out with 504 from proxy.

omar: joining bridge. can you post the query?

michelle: query: `sum(rate(tokenizer_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(tokenizer_requests_total[5m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(tokenizer_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))`.

kevin: TY. rolling up: customer-reported timeouts seen in support tickets for EU customers, CS alerted.

tara: is there an immediate mitigation we can flip? circuit to fallback variant?

michelle: plan: 1) scale tokenizer workers + bump batch-size timeout threshold 2) enable routing fallback to model-variant-lite (lower perf, more stable) for eu-west for affected routes 3) if that fails, shift a portion of traffic to us-west as emergency fallback (will increase latency for some customers). doing step 1 now.

ops-bot: runbook action triggered by @michelle — scaling tokenizer-deployment eu-west-1 to 12 replicas.

michelle: scaled to 12. waiting 90s for pods to warm.

jessica: will notify top 5 impacted customers via CS now. @cs-bot can you draft message?

cs-bot: Drafting notice: "We are seeing degraded streaming responses for EU customers; mitigation in progress. No data loss. Temporary routing changes may increase latency for some requests. Support will follow up." Sending to CS team for approval. :email:

michelle: pods warming helped p95 but p99 still elevated. proceeding to step 2 — enable model-variant-lite fallback for route `/v1/stream` for eu-west.

kevin: config snippet (will apply as feature-flag):
```
route: /v1/stream
routing:
  eu-west-1:
    - weight: 80
      variant: standard
    - weight: 20
      variant: lite-fallback
```

michelle: feature flag applied. traffic shifting. observing.

michelle: good — errors dropping to ~0.5% and streaming restored for most requests. customer errors still trickling.

omar: should we keep this until root cause identified? also need to hand off to next oncall.

michelle: yes. leaving fallback enabled. recording mitigation steps in incident doc. handoff to @omar for post-incident follow-up and postmortem owner.

michelle: oncall handoff: I am clear; bridge + logs in #incidents. Omar take it from here.

omar: taking over. thanks @michelle. I'll coordinate the postmortem and action tracking.

omar: quick customer-impact note for PMs/CS: affected customers: 5 accounts with elevated error rates (IDs redacted in-thread). Estimated customer-impact window: 2026-10-09T14:23:00Z — 2026-10-09T15:01:00Z (primary mitigation effective at ~14:38 UTC).

kevin: filing an incident ticket in tracker. link: https://issuetracker.redwood/INC-2026-457.

omar: postmortem scheduling: proposing 2026-10-12 15:00 UTC (30m). @tara please confirm availability for SRE/Platform.

tara: available. will bring runtime perf traces and KV-cache metrics.

jessica: CS will prepare customer timeline + ticket list.

omar: action items (initial):
- "A1: Tune tokenizer batcher thresholds to avoid p99 spikes" — owner: @kevin — due: 2026-10-16
- "A2: Add a safe-fallback routing flag for streaming endpoints (automated rollback)" — owner: @tara — due: 2026-10-20
- "A3: Alert tuning: require sustained >2% 5xx for 10m before paging; add a suppression window and de-dup by topology" — owner: @michelle — due: 2026-10-13
- "A4: Postmortem write-up and blame-free timeline" — owner: @omar — due: 2026-10-14
- "A5: Customer comms summary and follow-up" — owner: @jessica (CS) — due: 2026-10-12

michelle: adding runbook/update: will change alert expression to use `increase(tokenizer_errors_total[10m]) / increase(tokenizer_requests_total[10m]) > 0.02` and add a 10m sustained condition. Also will add a 15m dedupe window on paging for this alert to reduce noise during flapping periods.

kevin: follow-up engineering notes: there is a case where very long sequences bypass the batcher heuristic and force many small batches causing high per-token overhead. I'll add an input-length gating rule to avoid small-batch blowup. (A1 covers this).

ops-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-457, linked postmortem draft, and added action items A1..A5 to tracker.

omar: for monitoring improvements beyond tuning: propose adding a derived metric `tokenizer_small_batch_rate` and an anomaly detector alert; also group alerts by cluster + route so we don't page for tenant-only blips. owner: @tara (work item planned).

jessica: customers notified, one customer escalated; CS handling callbacks.

michelle: final check — errors stable at ~0.3% for 30m. leaving fallback enabled until A2 is implemented.

omar: noted. postmortem scheduled. I'll create the slack thread summary and link it in the ticket. thanks all for fast mitigation. :tada:

kevin: quick ops follow: can we add a CI load test covering long-sequence inputs with tokenizer profiling? putting on my plate after A1.

tara: will start a runbook PR for the routing fallback toggles so oncall can flip safely without manual config edits.

jessica: once postmortem is done CS will send customer follow-up and an FAQ for impacted teams.

omar: closing bridge. next steps tracked in INC-2026-457 and postmortem doc. if anyone sees regression, re-paging as normal.

sre-bot: Bridge closed by @omar at 2026-10-09T15:10:25Z.

michelle: thanks team.
